gates.label: Remote API origin, secret, and privacy boundary
gates.requirement: Before public activation, the deployed hah.dev origin must expose exactly one named same-origin POST /api/lattice capability. After explicit confirmation and under one origin-wide browser Web Lock, the canonical client must first send a bodyless visitor-session setup with Accept application/vnd.hah.text-to-lattice-visitor-session.v1+json and no Content-Type, then after an accepted 204 setup send exactly one content-bearing request with schema version 1 and only text, requested_mode, and schema_version in its body. A transport or non-204 setup failure must stop before the content request. Client script cannot observe storage of the HttpOnly cookie, so an accepted 204 whose cookie is blocked or dropped may still be followed by that one content request; the Worker must reject a missing cookie as 428 visitor_session_required before Durable Object admission or provider work, while invalid or undeclared cookies fail closed as 403 invalid_request at the same boundary. The setup must establish or preserve the signed cookie without a quota claim or provider call. The API Worker must use exactly the encrypted HF_TOKEN and VISITOR_COOKIE_SECRET bindings; a first isolated setup has no Cookie header, the following content request may carry only the signed opaque __Secure-hah-lattice-api-visitor cookie, and the setup response sets only that cookie with Path=/api/lattice, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, no Domain, and expiry at the next UTC-day boundary. No cookie value may enter retained evidence. The Worker must also use the fixed Hugging Face router and Featherless-qualified Qwen and Llama targets, bounded non-reflective errors, Cache-Control: no-store, no application content storage or logging, no automatic retry, no alternate provider or model fallback, and a Content-Security-Policy whose connect-src is 'self'.

gates.label: Remote provider capacity and cost boundary
gates.requirement: The bodyless visitor-session setup must make no quota claim and no provider call. A content request with no cookie must fail 428 visitor_session_required, while one with an invalid, tampered, or undeclared cookie must fail 403 invalid_request, before Durable Object admission or provider work in either case. After exact content-request validation and before provider work, the deployed API must make exactly one atomic admission claim and accept at most 30 transformations globally per UTC day and 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day. Intentional cookie clearing and uncooperative callers remain outside the per-browser identity claim; the global 30-per-day counter remains exact and authoritative. An admitted attempt counts even if its caller disconnects or provider work later fails; it is never refunded and encounters no second shared quota claim within its pipeline. Quota identity and state use no IP address, browser fingerprint, submitted content, or result. Each admitted request permits at most 32 provider calls, so admitted requests expose at most 960 provider calls per UTC day. The path-scoped Worker rate limiter remains a 30-per-60-second edge shaper; per-call time and response size remain bounded, with no paid or generic proxy path and no promise of provider rate, retention, availability, or cost behavior.
gates.currentEvidence: Deterministic source contracts bound per-visitor and global admission, lease lifetime, retry behavior, row lifecycle, and fail-closed provider errors. Under the public reusable testing token, however, one client can use the permitted 16-request acquisition sequence to fill all eight slots and renew them; the 48-per-10-second per-IP rule does not stop that sequence. The controls bound cost, state, and privacy consequence, not tool availability, and source cannot establish live provider capacity.

That response must set exactly the __Secure-hah-lattice-api-visitor cookie with Path=/api/lattice, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, no Domain, and a Max-Age within the next UTC-day boundary. Under the same lock, after an accepted 204 the client must then produce exactly one content-bearing same-origin POST /api/lattice with only text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1 in its body and only that browser-owned cookie, then reach one non-error terminal result (translated, conformant-for-context, or review-required). A transport or non-204 setup failure must stop before the content request. Because script cannot observe HttpOnly-cookie storage, an accepted 204 whose cookie is blocked or dropped may still be followed by that one content request; the missing-cookie request must fail 428 visitor_session_required before admission and provider work. Setup must consume no transformation quota and make no provider call. Neither request carries an account, authorization, or provider credential. The trace must show no provider origin contacted by the browser, no automatic retry, no service-worker replay or cache replay, and no additional content-bearing browser request, and must distinguish the intentionally transmitted request body from prohibited source or result reflection in URLs, headers, errors, logs, caches, analytics, and unrelated traffic. marginalValueDecisionScopes.claimBoundary: Historical-inactive decisions remain verbatim evidence of the superseded browser-local boundary. They neither qualify nor constrain the active remote candidate except as recorded design history.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Leading-zero Retry-After inflation
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: A standards-valid ordinary response could inflate denial time; canonicalization is bounded and reusable.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Pre-1900 HTTP-date rejection
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: The provider is not expected to emit such a date and the consequence is bounded, but completed work is not rolled back.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Keyword-only prohibited-topic blocking
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: It would block legitimate quotation, journalism, criticism, fiction, prevention, and defensive analysis while remaining easy to evade. Purpose-and-consequence evaluation has greater fidelity and lower lifecycle burden.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Deterministic language detection as the sole Llama-language gate
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Short, mixed, named-entity-heavy, and transliterated text makes bespoke detection unreliable; a point-of-use supported-language confirmation is bounded and auditable.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Machine-enforced release-state boundary
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Every main-branch publication otherwise risks activating a known open release blocker or diverging from the reviewed qualification state.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Byte-for-byte reconstruction of the undocumented historical WASM build
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Exact artifact identity, integrity, lineage, ABI, and configuration are already bound. Reconstructing missing workstation state adds bespoke build and maintenance burden without a commensurate plausible failure reduction; upstream clarification or a maintainable controlled replacement remains useful.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Immediate post-deployment official-page acquisition, terminal conversion, release, and privacy trace
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Failed declared-profile acquisition, failure before a non-error terminal conversion, failed release, conditional analytics injection, or sensitive prose leaving the browser would have meaningful consequences. The earlier Safari/WebKit and Brave/Chromium records remain historical lifecycle and privacy evidence for their deployed revision but did not establish a terminal conversion, and the 2026-09-11 owner report records that the first repaired runtime still produced no terminal result. After the replacement source candidate deploys, repeat the official-page lifecycle and privacy review, bind one supported-browser terminal result to that deployed revision, verify browser-shaped responses contain no Cloudflare beacon or RUM marker, and return to held publication on failure; testing-profile success remains narrower than anti-bot evidence, and source no-transform policy does not prove provider analytics is disabled.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Deliberately timed real-browser renewal trace
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: A real renewal defect could affect a long session, but source and adversarial tests cover renewal timing, bodyless PATCH behavior, fail-closed local termination, bounded lease expiry, and eventual cleanup. Record renewal when an ordinary session reaches the interval and roll back on an observed defect; deliberately waiting or building a harness adds little incremental assurance and must not hold operational completion.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Response-policy enforcement despite the static GitHub Pages origin
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Missing CSP and Permissions-Policy would expose the main document to a realistic cross-origin and runtime-expansion failure. A small exact-path edge policy is reusable, live-verifiable, and removes that consequential deployment gap without changing the static origin.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Portfolio-wide response-policy Worker route
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Attaching hah.dev/* would couple unrelated portfolio pages and traffic to a Text to Lattice-specific Worker, consume its request allowance, and expand the failure blast radius. Four exact document routes plus the in-document CSP fallback protect the authorized launch surfaces with lower lifecycle and reliability cost.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Cloudflare official testing credentials for the demonstrable release
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: A real hostname-restricted widget would reduce automated capacity abuse, but no such pair has been supplied and qualified for this release, while indefinite unavailability would defeat the authorized demonstrator. Cloudflare's documented testing pair can exercise the official browser widget and Siteverify flow, while the direct preactivation probe establishes only Siteverify, lease, and release behavior. Explicit disclosure, exact-origin and bodyless boundaries, independent signing domains, per-location shaping, global daily admission, concurrent-lease caps, and bounded expiry contain financial, privacy, and state consequence but do not assure availability. It must not be represented as production anti-bot assurance.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Bespoke attestation bypass route or unsigned token mode
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: A new bypass endpoint or unsigned client assertion would add an undocumented public protocol, attack surface, and maintenance path. The provider's exact published test profile is narrower, recognizable, replaceable, and remains inside the existing Siteverify and signed-lease contract, even though its reusable dummy token can be sent without proving widget participation.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Public testing-token slot starvation and the 48-per-10-second edge rule
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: One client can use the allowed 16-request acquisition sequence to fill all eight slots and keep renewing them with the reusable public dummy token; the 48-per-10-second per-IP rule does not prevent that plausible sequence. The exact caps, four-hour lifetime, fail-closed free tier, browser-local prose, and no-paid-overage boundary limit consequence to demonstrator availability, which the interface does not assure. The edge rule remains recommended defense in depth under GATE-03, and observed abuse triggers requalification rather than a false pre-release anti-bot claim.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Held résumé title and Text to Lattice icon link drift
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: A stale built-boundary assertion could reject the corrected canonical-title and SVG-only tool-link contract. The mismatch was plausible after the interaction change and cheap to fix without weakening the hold.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Shared verification-frame propagation deadline
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: A slowly settling first asset could leave later healthy frame assets only a token verification window and create a recoverable deployment false negative. Independent bounded windows are cheap and improve lifecycle reliability.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Pinned Workerd redirect incompatibility in the Siteverify subrequest
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: The deployed runtime rejected redirect:error before Siteverify ran, making every realistic acquisition fail with HTTP 403. Manual redirect handling restores interoperability while the response validator still rejects and cancels every 3xx; a regression binds that fail-closed behavior.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Replay of an ambiguous live lease acquisition probe
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Retrying a non-idempotent grant after a transient response or timeout could consume more than one lease and obscure the production result. A single bounded acquisition attempt is cheap, prevents verifier-created capacity leakage, and leaves ordinary idempotent deployment probes retryable.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Simultaneous programmatic résumé-modal body-class race
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Normal interface paths cannot open two résumé modals at once. Reference-counting a shared body class would add coordination complexity for a programmatic-only, nonconsequential state.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Remote privacy boundary before activation
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: The migration intentionally transmits user text through a new same-origin API and external provider. Source controls cannot prove the deployed route, secret binding, edge policy, retention behavior, or canonical-browser trace, so activation before GATE-02, GATE-03, and GATE-06 close would create a false privacy qualification.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Provider-managed revision and historical byte equivalence
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: The fixed provider-qualified model identifiers constrain routing, but the provider-managed runtime is not byte-pinned and is not established as equivalent to historical MLC artifacts. Publishing that boundary and reopening qualification on target or provider drift has greater lifecycle value than claiming unavailable byte identity.

marginalValueDecisions.finding: Automatic retry or alternate provider or model fallback
marginalValueDecisions.rationale: Automatic replay would retransmit visitor text without a new deliberate action, while fallback would silently expand recipients and model behavior. Explicit finite failure preserves consent, privacy, predictability, and auditability.
